facts.value: SEK 3,800–4,350/month for a corridor room or room in a shared flat (KTH student budget examples, 2026); Stockholm University budget assumes SEK 6,500/month.

facts.value: 1-bedroom flat: ~SEK 10,640/month outside centre, ~SEK 15,770 in centre (Nov 2026). KTH Housing example: SEK 8,200/month.
SEK 7,850–13,000/month incl. rent (KTH 2026 student examples); Stockholm University estimate SEK 12,000/month.
facts.source_name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology – student budget 2026

facts.value: SL 30-day ticket at student (reduced) price: SEK 650 in KTH 2026 budget; SEK 325 during the half-price campaign (buy/activate by 2 Dec 2026). Full-time students only.
Mean temperature about −1.0 °C in January and 18.7 °C in July; about 546 mm precipitation/year (SMHI 1991–2020, Observatorielunden).
facts.notes: Wikipedia climate table citing SMHI 1991–2020 normals; SMHI's own tables were not reached.

facts.value: Parks, waterfronts and museums (many free or discounted for students); KTH's student union THS runs many clubs and an August–September welcome for internationals.
Swedish not needed for daily life (Swedes speak English widely); some part-time jobs require Swedish, others are offered in English.
Part-time work possible but full-time study is ~40 h/week; KTH sometimes hires students as teaching/lab assistants or ambassadors. Non-EU permit holders: max 15 h/week.
No city data. National example: hotel/restaurant agreement floor SEK 153.64–164.30/hour (from 1 Apr 2026, no experience; youth rates under 20). No statutory minimum wage.
facts.source_name: HRF (Hotel and Restaurant Workers' Union) – Gröna Riksavtalet
facts.notes: A collective-agreement wage floor for one sector, not a measured typical student wage; no citable source for typical student pay found.
